newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened mildly in quiet trading on Wednesday against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies after the Bank of Israel intervened in the market to buy dollars, dealers said.

"The Bank of Israel is continuing its policy of buying dollars just before it sets the daily representative rate to keep the basket at seven percent below the midpoint of the trading band," said Ilan Zadka at United Mizrahi Bank.
"The basket was almost unchanged today and the shekel weakened slightly against the dollar following the dollar's rise in Europe," Zadka said.

The shekel is allowed to trade in a band of seven percent above or below a sloping midpoint designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.1910 against 3.1880 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5614 shekels against 3.5609 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.860 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8674 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0851 shekels per mark against 2.0896 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1910 shekels.
